correctness.rationale: For every finite triangle-free base, the Henson extension property identifies complete injective types with labelled triangle-free finite extensions. Direct case analysis on one/two/three new vertices proves t1=I, t2=I^2+C and t3=I^3+3IC+3J. Exact independent-neighborhood augmentation and degree-group canonical encoding enumerate all and only isomorphism classes through 7 vertices (class counts 1,1,2,3,7,14,38,107). Direct exact bitmask calculations find a single class of size 2 with (I,C)=(36,597), no earlier collision; transfer matrices independently give J=11545 and 11519 and hence t3=145767 and 145689. Adding isolated old vertices has exact factors I:2, C:3, J:5, proving a 78*5^k tertiary gap for all k>=0. The bundled standalone verifier was executed against actual staged files, and an independent NetworkX atlas enumeration corroborated the finite census.

value.rationale: Low-arity orbit-number reconstruction is a natural model-theoretic question: how much of a pointwise-named finite base is retained by numerical parameter-type spectra? The unique minimum failure and exact seven-vertex classification identify a sharp threshold rather than a chosen arbitrary small slice, and the infinite isolate-padding family proves that a third-arity count can remain essential at unbounded sizes. This links independent-set and graph-homomorphism partition functions to a concrete structural distinction; not merely a restatement of a general enumeration formula.
